q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, which of the following budget reviews has been dispensed with?
e: After the Railway Budget merged with the General Budget, the August Review was dispensed with; the budget is now reviewed only at the Revised Estimates stage in September and the Final Modification stage in January.

q: The final review of the Budget during a financial year, carried out in January, is called:
e: The Final Modification Estimates, prepared in January, are the last review of the year's budget, when grants are finally modified to match the likely actual expenditure of the year.

q: The Revised Estimates and the Budget Estimates for the ensuing year are prepared in September, broadly on the basis of actuals of the first:
e: The Revised Estimates and the next year's Budget Estimates are framed in September, broadly on the basis of the actuals of the first five months of the current financial year.

q: The Ordinary Working Expenses of Indian Railways are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Ordinary Working Expenses of the Railways are accounted for under Major Head 3002; Major Head 3001 covers policy formulation and direction, while 5002 covers capital outlay.

q: Amounts credited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF) are primarily utilised for:

options.A: Payment of pension to retired staff
options.B: Renewal and replacement of railway assets
options.D: Meeting the dividend liability to General Finances

e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is built up by appropriations from revenue and is utilised mainly to finance renewal and replacement of assets that have worn out or become obsolete.

q: Re-appropriation means:

options.A: Obtaining a fresh grant from Parliament during the year
options.B: Transfer of funds from one primary unit/sub-head to another within the same grant by the competent authority
options.C: Surrender of the entire grant at the end of the year
options.D: Charging expenditure to a suspense head temporarily

e: Re-appropriation is the transfer of funds from one primary unit or sub-head to another within the same grant by the competent authority, without approaching Parliament for a fresh grant.

q: Where the amount provided in the sanctioned budget for a service is found insufficient during the year, the additional requirement is met through:

options.B: Contingency Fund advance, never to be recouped
options.D: Token grant from the Public Account

e: Where the sanctioned provision for a service proves insufficient during the year, the additional requirement is met through Supplementary Demands for Grants voted by Parliament during the year itself.

q: At the central level, the earnings of Indian Railways are accounted for with the Reserve Bank of India at its Central Accounts Section located at:
e: At the central level, railway earnings are accounted for with the Reserve Bank of India at its Central Accounts Section located at Nagpur.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure on a 'New Service' not contemplated in the approved budget requires the approval of Parliament.
2. A 'token grant' is taken when funds can be found by re-appropriation but the expenditure is on a new service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a new service not contemplated in the budget requires Parliament's approval, and where funds can be found by re-appropriation, only a token grant is taken for that new service.

q: The Capital Outlay on Indian Railways is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Indian Railways is accounted for under Major Head 5002, whereas the revenue working expenses are accounted for under Major Head 3002.

q: An item of expenditure is found to pertain to a head of account for which there is no budget provision. The correct course is to:

options.A: Book it to some other head where provision exists
options.B: Book it to its correct head of account, as classification is not governed by the availability of budget provision
options.C: Keep it under a suspense head permanently
options.D: Drop the item from the accounts altogether

e: An item must be booked to its correct head of account; classification follows the nature of the expenditure and is never governed by whether budget provision happens to exist under that head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A change in the classification (allocation) of expenditure takes effect only from the next financial year.
2. A change in classification can be applied retrospectively to the closed accounts of past years.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: a change in classification takes effect only from the next financial year. Statement 2 is wrong, as the closed accounts of past years cannot be reopened or restated.

q: The erstwhile revenue Demands for Grants 3 to 14 are now represented, under Major Head 3002, as:
e: Under Major Head 3002, the erstwhile revenue Demands 3 to 14 are represented in sequence as Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12, preserving the functional grouping of the working expenses.

q: Major Head 3001 of the railway accounts covers:

options.C: Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction, Research and other Miscellaneous Organisations
options.D: Transactions of the Railway Safety Fund

e: Major Head 3001 covers Indian Railways - Policy Formulation, Direction, Research and other Miscellaneous Organisations; working expenses fall under 3002 and capital outlay under 5002.

q: In the classification of railway expenditure, the 'Primary Units' represent:

options.A: The zonal railways incurring the expenditure
options.B: The objects of expenditure, such as pay, allowances and materials
options.D: The funds from which expenditure is met

e: Primary Units are the object heads of classification - they show what the money is spent on, such as pay, allowances, fuel and materials, under each sub-head of demand.

q: The Railway Safety Fund (RSF) is credited mainly with:

options.C: Appropriations from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

e: The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares, and its resources are earmarked for safety works.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) was created to finance:

options.B: Safety-related works, including renewal and replacement of safety assets

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) was created to finance safety-related works, such as renewal and replacement of track, signalling and other safety assets.

q: The Development Fund of the Railways is ordinarily used for works relating to:

options.A: Passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvements

e: The Development Fund, fed by appropriations from the revenue surplus, is ordinarily used for works of passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvements.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Pension Fund is credited with amounts appropriated from revenue.
2. Pension payments to retired staff are debited to the Pension Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Pension Fund is credited with amounts appropriated from revenue, and pension payments to retired staff are met by debit to the Pension Fund.

q: The Debt Service Fund on Indian Railways was set up for:

options.A: Servicing the debt obligations arising out of market borrowings
options.B: Meeting the cost of stores purchases

e: The Debt Service Fund was set up to service the debt obligations arising out of market borrowings, so that interest and repayment liabilities are met in an orderly manner.

q: A 'Vote on Account' is taken from Parliament to:

options.A: Regularise excess expenditure of the previous year
options.B: Authorise expenditure for the initial part of a financial year, pending approval of the full budget

e: A Vote on Account authorises expenditure for the initial part of a financial year, pending Parliament's approval of the full budget and the passing of the Appropriation Act.

q: 'Exchequer control' over railway expenditure is concerned with:

options.B: Regulating the pace of expenditure during the year in accordance with the availability of funds
options.C: Auditing the accounts after the year ends

e: Exchequer control means regulating the pace of expenditure during the year in accordance with the availability of funds, so that spending does not outrun the resources in hand.

q: Re-appropriation of funds is NOT permissible:

options.A: Between two primary units within the same sub-head of a grant
options.B: Within the same grant, with the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: From one grant (Demand) to another grant
options.D: Before the end of the financial year

e: Re-appropriation is confined within a single grant; funds cannot be transferred from one grant (Demand) to another, since each grant is voted separately by Parliament.

q: In the railway accounting system, transactions are first recorded in detail in the:
e: Transactions are first recorded in detail in the subsidiary books of the originating offices; their classified summaries are then posted into the General Books.

q: The Account Current rendered by a zonal railway is:

options.A: A daily statement of cash at stations
options.B: A monthly account of the railway rendered to the Railway Board
options.C: An annual statement of stores balances
options.D: A statement of passenger earnings only

e: The Account Current is the monthly account of the railway rendered to the Railway Board, summarising the receipts, expenditure and balances of the railway for the month.

q: The Debt Head Report (DHR) shows:

options.A: The staff strength of the Accounts Department
options.B: The details of capital works in progress
options.C: The earnings of the railway for the month
options.D: The balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account

e: The Debt Head Report shows the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account, so that items awaiting final adjustment remain under watch.

q: A balance under the head 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents:

options.A: Earnings collected at stations but not remitted
options.B: The cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Loans taken from the Reserve Bank

e: A balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents the cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank of India, against which payments are made.

q: 'Cash-in-Transit' in railway accounts represents:

options.A: Cash held in the station chest
options.C: Earnings collected but not yet deposited with, or credited by, the bank

e: Cash-in-Transit represents earnings collected at stations and other offices but not yet deposited with, or credited by, the bank - the money is still in transit.

q: A credit balance under the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' indicates:

options.B: Cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank
options.D: Excess cash with the cash office

e: A credit balance under 'Cheques and Bills' indicates cheques issued and treated as paid in the books but not yet actually paid by the bank, so the amount remains outstanding.

q: 'E-Recon' in railway accounts refers to:

options.A: Electronic reconciliation of inter-railway transfer transactions

e: E-Recon is the electronic reconciliation of inter-railway transfer transactions, matching the debits raised by one railway with the corresponding credits of the other railway.

q: Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the Budget (including Railways) is presented to Parliament on:

options.A: The last working day of February

e: Since the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the Budget including Railways is presented to Parliament on 1 February, ahead of the new financial year.

q: The Appropriation Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha:

options.A: After the Demands for Grants have been voted
options.B: Before the general discussion on the Budget
options.D: Only after the Appropriation Accounts are ready

e: The Appropriation Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha only after the Demands for Grants have been voted, to authorise withdrawal of the voted and charged amounts from the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: Expenditure incurred in excess of a sanctioned grant during a year is ultimately regularised by:

options.A: Excess Grants voted by Parliament after the close of the year
options.C: A supplementary demand in the following year's budget

e: Expenditure incurred in excess of a sanctioned grant is regularised after the close of the year by Excess Grants voted by Parliament on the basis of the Appropriation Accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it can be discussed.
2. Charged expenditure is also authorised through the Appropriation Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it can be discussed, and it is also authorised through the Appropriation Act.

q: The payment of dividend by the Railways to General Finances was dispensed with from the financial year:
e: With the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the payment of dividend by the Railways to General Finances was dispensed with from the financial year 2017-18.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) is the budgetary support extended to the Railways through the Union Budget.
2. Extra Budgetary Resources (EBR) are raised from the market and their servicing is the responsibility of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Gross Budgetary Support is the support extended through the Union Budget, while Extra Budgetary Resources are raised from the market and their servicing is the Railways' own responsibility.

q: Which fund was created in 1993-94 to finance capital works of the Railways out of their own internal resources?
e: The Capital Fund was created in 1993-94 to finance capital works of the Railways out of their own internal resources, reducing dependence on budgetary support.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), announced in the Budget 2017-18, was proposed with a corpus of:

options.C: Rs 1,00,000 crore in a single year

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, announced in the Budget 2017-18, was proposed with a corpus of Rs 1,00,000 crore to be built up over five years for critical safety works.

q: The Railway Safety Fund is utilised mainly for works relating to:

options.D: Level crossings and road over/under bridges

e: The Railway Safety Fund is utilised mainly for works relating to level crossings and road over-bridges and road under-bridges, where road traffic crosses the railway track.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is treated as a part of the working expenses of the Railways.
2. The Depreciation Reserve Fund is financed by grants-in-aid from the Contingency Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is treated as a part of the working expenses. Statement 2 is wrong - the fund is fed from railway revenue, not by grants-in-aid from the Contingency Fund.

q: Which of the following is NOT a fund of the Indian Railways?
e: The Contingency Fund of India is a fund of the Union Government, not a railway fund; the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund and Pension Fund are the Railways' own funds.

q: The aggregate capital invested in the Railways, forming the base of its capital structure, is known as:
e: Capital-at-charge is the aggregate capital invested in the Railways, which forms the base of its capital structure and on which dividend was historically computed.

q: The erstwhile Demand No. 16 of the separate Railway Budget related to:

options.A: Capital expenditure — acquisition, construction and replacement of assets

e: Erstwhile Demand No. 16 of the separate Railway Budget related to capital expenditure - the acquisition, construction and replacement of assets - as distinct from the revenue demands.

q: Plan Head 31 in the Railways' investment classification stands for:
e: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Plan Head 31 stands for Track Renewals; Rolling Stock is Plan Head 21 and New Lines is Plan Head 11.

q: Plan Head 21 in the Railways' investment classification stands for:
e: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, Plan Head 21 stands for Rolling Stock - locomotives, coaches, wagons and other rail vehicles.

q: In the Primary Unit (object) classification, stores issued to revenue works are accounted for under Primary Unit:
e: Stores issued to revenue works are accounted for under Primary Unit 27, the object head prescribed for stores consumed on revenue account.

q: Material consumed on periodical overhaul (POH) of the home railway's rolling stock in workshops is accounted for under Primary Unit:
e: Material consumed on periodical overhaul (POH) of the home railway's own rolling stock in workshops is accounted for under Primary Unit 35.

q: The cost of an addition or betterment which materially enhances the capacity or value of an existing asset is chargeable to:
e: An addition or betterment that materially enhances the capacity or value of an existing asset is capital in nature, hence chargeable to Capital or the Development Fund, not to ordinary repairs.

q: In the classification of railway accounts, the head immediately below a Sub-Major Head is the:
e: In the classification hierarchy, the head immediately below a Sub-Major Head is the Minor Head, followed further below by the sub-head and the detailed head.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The classification of a transaction is determined by the nature of the transaction, and not by the fund or source from which it is financed.
2. A capital work financed from the Development Fund is therefore classified under revenue heads.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: classification is determined by the nature of the transaction, not by its source of finance. Statement 2 is wrong - a capital work financed from the Development Fund is still classified under the capital heads.

q: Balances of the State Railway Provident Fund in the railway accounts are shown under the group:
e: Balances of the State Railway Provident Fund are shown under the Debt heads, since the fund money belongs to the subscribers and represents a liability of the Railways.

q: An error of classification in the accounts, detected during the same financial year, is corrected through:
e: An error of classification detected during the same financial year is corrected through transfer (journal) entries, which shift the amount from the wrong head to the correct head.

q: A suspense head is operated in the books when:

options.A: The amount involved is very large
options.B: The Accounts Officer is on leave
options.C: It is desired to keep the item permanently out of the classified accounts
options.D: The final head of account cannot be determined at the time of booking the transaction

e: A suspense head is operated when the final head of account cannot be determined at the time of booking the transaction, so the item is held temporarily till its classification is settled.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The General Books of a railway are posted from the classified summaries of the subsidiary books.
2. The monthly Account Current is compiled from the General Books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the General Books are posted from the classified summaries of the subsidiary books, and the monthly Account Current is compiled from the General Books.

q: The bank accredited for conducting the banking business of the Railways — collection of earnings and disbursements — is the:
e: The State Bank of India is the bank accredited for conducting the banking business of the Railways, including collection of earnings and disbursements on their behalf.

q: A balance under the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' represents:

options.A: Cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised
options.B: Cash held by the Cash & Pay Office
options.C: Cheques issued but not yet paid

e: A balance under 'Remittances into Banks' represents cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised, so the credit has been taken but realisation is still awaited.

q: The suspense head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' differs from 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in that it represents:

options.A: The actual cash balance held with the Reserve Bank
options.B: Transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank, pending the Bank's advice
options.C: Loans advanced by the Reserve Bank
options.D: Station earnings held in cash chests

e: 'Reserve Bank Suspense' represents transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank, pending the Bank's advice, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' is the actual cash balance held with the Bank.

q: Under the 'focal point' system of remittance of station earnings:

options.A: Each station deals directly with the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.B: Stations remit their earnings only once a month
options.C: Earnings are retained at stations till the close of the year
options.D: Earnings of a group of stations are remitted to, and accounted at, nominated focal point branches of the accredited bank

e: Under the focal point system, earnings of a group of stations are remitted to, and accounted at, nominated focal point branches of the accredited bank, instead of each station dealing with the bank separately.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transfer transactions between two units of the same railway are adjusted within the books of that railway itself.
2. Inter-railway transfer transactions are settled through the books of the Railway Board.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: transfer transactions between units of the same railway are adjusted within that railway's own books, while inter-railway transfers are settled through the books of the Railway Board.

q: A debit raised by one railway against another railway in a transfer transaction is intimated through a:
e: A debit raised by one railway against another in a transfer transaction is intimated through a Transfer Certificate, on the strength of which the other railway accepts the debit.

q: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the railways over which the traffic passes is made broadly in proportion to:

options.A: The originating earnings of each railway
options.B: The distance (lead) traversed over each railway
options.C: The wagon fleet owned by each railway
options.D: The number of stations on each railway

e: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings is made among the railways over which the traffic passes, broadly in proportion to the distance (lead) traversed over each railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Apportionment is required only for through traffic which passes over more than one railway.
2. Earnings of local traffic belong wholly to the railway on which the traffic is booked and carried.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: apportionment is required only for through traffic passing over more than one railway, and earnings of local traffic belong wholly to the railway on which it is booked and carried.

q: The net effect of apportionment on the total earnings of the Indian Railways taken as a whole is:

options.A: Nil — it only redistributes the earnings among the railways concerned
options.D: It converts revenue earnings into capital receipts

e: Apportionment only redistributes the same through-traffic earnings among the railways concerned, so its net effect on the total earnings of the Indian Railways taken as a whole is nil.

q: 'Budget proportions' in railway budgeting are used for:

options.A: Fixing the proportions of salary and allowances of staff
options.B: Distributing among zonal railways such expenditure (e.g., Railway Board and audit expenses) as is not directly attributable to any single railway
options.C: Deciding the proportion of voted and charged expenditure

e: Budget proportions are used for distributing among zonal railways such expenditure as is not directly attributable to a single railway, for example the expenses of the Railway Board and audit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Re-appropriation between the voted and charged portions of a grant is not permissible.
2. Re-appropriation from Capital to Revenue, or vice versa, is not permissible.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: re-appropriation between the voted and charged portions of a grant is not permissible, and neither is re-appropriation from Capital to Revenue or vice versa.

q: Re-appropriation of funds CANNOT be resorted to for meeting expenditure on:

options.A: A sanctioned work within the same grant
options.B: Another primary unit within the same grant
options.C: A work for which savings exist elsewhere in the grant
options.D: A new service not included in the approved budget

e: Re-appropriation can only rearrange funds within approved services; it cannot be used for a new service not included in the approved budget, which needs Parliament's sanction.

q: The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways compare the actual expenditure of the year with:

options.C: The Final Grant — the original grant as modified by supplementary grants and other modifications
options.D: The Budget Estimates of the following year

e: The Appropriation Accounts compare the actual expenditure of the year with the Final Grant - the original grant as modified by supplementary grants and other modifications - so that excesses and savings stand explained.

q: Funds provided in the budget which are expected to remain unutilised should be:

options.A: Retained till the last day of the financial year
options.B: Surrendered as soon as the savings are foreseen
options.C: Spent on any other work chosen by the officer
options.D: Carried forward automatically to the next year

e: Funds provided in the budget which are expected to remain unutilised should be surrendered as soon as the savings are foreseen, so that the money can be put to other use.

q: The 'Pink Book' of the Railways contains:

options.B: The earnings budget of the Railways
options.D: The Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes — the list of works included in the budget

e: The Pink Book contains the Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes - the list of works included in the budget, with their costs and allotments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A 'New Service' means a service which was not contemplated in the approved budget.
2. A 'New Instrument of Service' means an important addition to, or extension of, an existing service arising from a new policy decision.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both definitions are correct: a New Service is one not contemplated in the approved budget, and a New Instrument of Service is an important addition to, or extension of, an existing service arising from a new policy decision.

q: In place of the earlier practice of rendering an Approximate Account Current followed by a final one, a zonal railway now renders:
e: In place of the earlier Approximate Account Current followed by a final one, a zonal railway now renders a single monthly Account Current to the Railway Board.

q: Extra Budgetary Resources through Institutional Finance — EBR(IF) — mobilised through IRFC are used mainly for financing:
e: Extra Budgetary Resources through Institutional Finance, mobilised through IRFC, are used mainly for financing the acquisition of rolling stock for the Railways.

q: The Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway is primarily responsible for:

options.B: Receipt and payment of cash on behalf of the railway

e: The Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway is primarily responsible for the receipt and payment of cash on behalf of the railway, including payment of passed bills and salaries.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is provided for through:

options.B: Two Demands — one Revenue and one Capital
options.D: No Demand, as the entire expenditure is charged

e: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is provided for through a single Demand for Grants.

q: In the Union Government accounts, railway funds like the DRF, Development Fund and Pension Fund are maintained as part of:

options.C: The Revenue section of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Accounts kept wholly outside the Government account

e: Railway funds like the DRF, Development Fund and Pension Fund are maintained as part of the Public Account of India in the Union Government accounts.

q: Under Major Head 3002, Repairs and Maintenance of Permanent Way and Works (erstwhile Demand No. 4) is classified under Sub-Major Head:
e: Under Major Head 3002, Repairs and Maintenance of Permanent Way and Works (erstwhile Demand No. 4) is Sub-Major Head 02, as Demands 3 to 14 map in sequence onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Operating Expenses — Fuel (erstwhile Demand No. 10) appears under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Operating Expenses - Fuel (erstwhile Demand No. 10) appears as Sub-Major Head 08 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Staff Welfare and Amenities (erstwhile Demand No. 11) is classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Staff Welfare and Amenities (erstwhile Demand No. 11) is Sub-Major Head 09 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Provident Fund, Pension and Other Retirement Benefits (erstwhile Demand No. 13) appear under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Provident Fund, Pension and Other Retirement Benefits (erstwhile Demand No. 13) appear as Sub-Major Head 11 under Major Head 3002, in the sequence mapping Demands 3 to 14 onto Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: Appropriations to the various Railway Funds (erstwhile Demand No. 14) are classified under Major Head 3002 as Sub-Major Head:
e: Appropriations to the various Railway Funds (erstwhile Demand No. 14) are classified as Sub-Major Head 12 under Major Head 3002, the last in the sequence of Sub-Major Heads 01 to 12.

q: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, 'New Lines' is Plan Head:
e: In the investment (Plan Head) classification, New Lines (construction) is Plan Head 11.

q: Road Safety Works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges are classified under Plan Head:
e: Road Safety Works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges are classified under Plan Head 30; works at level crossings fall under Plan Head 29.

q: Workshops, including production units, are classified under Plan Head:
e: Workshops, including production units, are classified under Plan Head 42 in the investment (Plan Head) classification.

q: Works of passenger amenities are classified under Plan Head:
e: Works of passenger amenities are classified under Plan Head 53 in the investment (Plan Head) classification.

q: The cost of replacing an existing asset by a similar asset, without material enhancement of its capacity, is chargeable to:

options.C: Ordinary revenue (working expenses) in all cases

e: The cost of replacing an existing asset by a similar asset, without material enhancement of its capacity, is a renewal chargeable to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, which exists to finance such replacements.

q: In the classification of a capital work, the source from which the work is financed (Capital, DRF, Development Fund, RRSK etc.) is indicated as its:
e: In the classification of a capital work, the Plan Head shows the type of work, while the source from which it is financed - Capital, DRF, Development Fund, RRSK and so on - is indicated as its Allocation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A track renewal work remains classified under Plan Head 31 whether it is financed from Capital or from the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
2. The fund financing a work determines the Plan Head under which the work is classified.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: a track renewal work remains under Plan Head 31 whether financed from Capital or from the DRF. Statement 2 is wrong - the financing source is shown only as the allocation and does not fix the Plan Head.

q: In railway accounts, all transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded in the:
e: In railway accounts, all transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded in the Journal Book, from where they are posted to the respective heads of account.

q: A journal (transfer) entry passed in the accounts must invariably show:

options.A: Only the head to be debited
options.B: Only the head to be credited
options.C: The name of the officer who prepared it, in place of the heads of account
options.D: Both the head to be debited and the head to be credited, with the reasons for the adjustment

e: A journal (transfer) entry must invariably show both the head to be debited and the head to be credited, with the reasons for the adjustment, so that the entry is complete and traceable.

q: The head-wise monthly summary of transactions prepared from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, is known as the:
e: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary of transactions prepared from the subsidiary books, and it is from this abstract that the General Books are posted.

q: All cash receipts and payments of a zonal railway effected through the Cash & Pay Office are recorded chronologically in the:
e: All cash receipts and payments effected through the Cash & Pay Office are recorded chronologically in the Main Cash Book, the primary record of cash transactions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An imprest is a standing advance of a fixed amount given to an officer to meet petty and contingent expenditure.
2. The imprest is recouped when the holder renders an account of the expenditure incurred out of it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: an imprest is a standing advance of a fixed amount for petty and contingent expenditure, and it is recouped when the holder renders an account of the expenditure incurred from it.

q: At any check of an imprest, the cash in hand with the holder plus the paid vouchers held by him should equal:

options.A: The sanctioned amount of the imprest
options.B: The expenditure incurred in the previous month
options.C: Half the annual contingent grant of the office
options.D: The balance shown in the Cash Book

e: At any check of an imprest, the cash in hand with the holder plus the paid vouchers held by him should together equal the sanctioned amount of the imprest.

q: The amount of an imprest sanctioned to an officer is fixed primarily with reference to:

options.C: The probable petty and contingent expenditure to be met from it
options.D: The number of staff working under him

e: The amount of an imprest is fixed primarily with reference to the probable petty and contingent expenditure to be met from it, so that it is adequate for the office's needs.

q: The outstanding items under each suspense head are watched through a register maintained for the purpose, known as the:
e: The outstanding items under each suspense head are watched through the Suspense Register, maintained so that each item can be pursued and cleared to its final head of account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under suspense heads are reviewed periodically so that the items are cleared by adjustment to the final heads of account as early as possible.
2. Suspense balances remaining outstanding at the close of the year are carried forward and reflected in the Debt Head Report.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: suspense balances are reviewed periodically so items are cleared to final heads as early as possible, and balances outstanding at the close of the year are carried forward and reflected in the Debt Head Report.

q:
Consider the following statements about balances under suspense heads:
1. A debit balance generally represents amounts paid or advanced which are awaiting recovery or final adjustment.
2. A credit balance generally represents amounts received or held which are awaiting disbursement or final adjustment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: a debit suspense balance generally represents amounts paid or advanced awaiting recovery or final adjustment, and a credit balance represents amounts received or held awaiting disbursement or final adjustment.

q: Budgetary control over expenditure in the Accounts Office is exercised mainly through the:

options.A: Budget Register, in which the allotments and the expenditure booked under each head are recorded

e: Budgetary control over expenditure in the Accounts Office is exercised mainly through the Budget Register, in which the allotments and the expenditure booked under each head are recorded.

q: Expenditure incurred in excess of the allotment available under a head, without prior sanction of re-appropriation or a supplementary grant, is treated as:
e: Expenditure incurred in excess of the allotment available under a head, without prior sanction by re-appropriation or a supplementary grant, is treated as unauthorised (irregular) expenditure.

q: The monthly financial review of a zonal railway primarily compares the actual earnings and expenditure of the period with:

options.A: The Budget Estimates and the proportionate allotment for the period
options.B: The actuals of the corresponding period of the previous year only
options.C: The Final Modification Estimates of the previous year
options.D: The estimates of the other zonal railways

e: The monthly financial review of a zonal railway primarily compares the actual earnings and expenditure of the period with the Budget Estimates and the proportionate allotment for the period.
